# PBSD port ledger

**Generated by `tools/port_plan.py`. Do not edit; re-run and commit the diff.**

One numbered entry per file PBSD owns, and per function in it. `docs/ROADMAP.md`
is the same work at the level of subsystems and is the one to read first; this
is the ledger you pick an item out of.

## How to read it

```
A       area       1..N, fixed order
A.D     directory  within the area, sorted by path
A.D.F   file       within the directory, sorted by name
A.D.F.N function   within the file, in source order
```

Numbers are positional. Inserting a file renumbers what follows, which is
fine because the ledger is regenerated rather than edited — **cite the path in
a commit message, never the number.**

| tag | meaning |
|---|---|
| `TODO-PORT` | C that PBSD intends to port to C++23. The default. |
| `TODO-ASM` | assembly: rewrite, drop, or reclassify `TODO-KEEP` per `docs/ASSEMBLY.md`. |
| `TODO-MD` | machine-dependent. Porting it starts with whether it should exist — `docs/CONSOLIDATION.md`. |
| `TODO-HDR` | a header. Follows its consumers rather than leading them. |
| `TODO-GEN` | generated. Porting the output is the wrong end. |
| `TODO-DATA` | a C file that is an array of numbers — firmware, tables, init values. Not a port. |
| `TODO-DECIDE` | a product decision before a porting one. |
| `SKIP-VENDOR` | `contrib/`, `crypto/`, `cddl/`. A local edit is a merge conflict for ever. |
| `SKIP-TESTS` | `tests/`. Runs against the port; is not part of it. |
| `DONE-MODULE` | unused — see the note on `pbsd/` below. |

**What is already ported is recorded per directory, not per file.** A heading
that says *N module(s) under `pbsd/lib/libc/stdio`* means the directory has
that many `.cppm` files; it does not say which of the sources below they
correspond to. The first version of this matched module names against source
names and reported 150 of `bin`'s 162 files as ported, because `pbsd/userland`
carries thousands of modules named after the symbol they wrap and `cat` is not
a unique name in a tree this size. Mapping `pbsd/userland`'s flat filenames
back to source paths is `docs/ROADMAP.md` §5, and is not something to guess
at in a ledger.

**The function list is a floor, not an inventory.** Names come from a regex for
a definition starting at column zero. Anything a macro generates is invisible to
it — arm64's `atomic.h` produces its entire interface that way and no regex will
ever see a single name. Where a file's `gen` count is high, read the file.
